title: Unnecessary Conversions and Hidden Clones
goal: Spot hidden string allocations like to_string() and to_owned() when references work.

sections.text: In languages like Python or Java, passing strings around never copies heap text because string objects are garbage-collected references.
In Rust, calling `.to_string()` or `.to_owned()` on a string slice `&str` allocates new memory on the heap and copies every byte.

sections.caption: The function parameter requires only a borrowed string slice.

sections.text: Calling `print_label(&name)` passes a borrow with zero allocations. Writing `print_label(&name.to_string())` allocates a temporary `String`, borrows it, and immediately drops it.

sections.caption: Converting a &str to String just to borrow it back as &str is a hidden clone.

sections.text: When designing APIs that only read string data, accept `&str` instead of `String`. That allows callers to pass string literals and borrowed slices without allocating.

explanation: Spot hidden string allocations like to_string() and to_owned() when references work.
